title: M1 library, admission, offline RSI, oracle, process, delivery and intake contracts v1

check_run.description: One mechanical or suite check that actually ran.

trial_file.description: Closed TrialFile; content_ref resolves to a controller artifact.

published_file.description: One file written under the destination. path is relative with no parent traversal.

admission_request.description: assess(): ask the policy-selected provider for an assurance decision. Identity is (candidate sha, policy sha, profile sha, request_id).

admission_decision.description: Provider output committed as the Verdict body. An RSI child (parent_decl_hash set) is always admitted_inactive. Puppet decisions run no suite.

library_snapshot_request.description: snapshot(request_id): librarian publishes the active selection atomically.

library_snapshot_result.description: Reply to snapshot(): ref of the committed library_snapshot.

library_snapshot.description: Frozen LibrarySnapshot. Entries are sorted by capability_name then decl_hash; no duplicate names or hashes in the active selection (checked at publication).

catalogue_request.description: catalogue(snapshot_ref): read-only listing for the isolated planner.

catalogue_result.description: Entries of the pinned snapshot, no redaction of contract fields.

activation_request.description: activate(): move the active alias to an admitted exact hash. Null expected_current_hash means no current pointer. Rollback uses the same request with an older admitted hash.

activation_record.description: Payload of the activation SystemRecord. It is authority; the alias projection can be rebuilt from it.

rsi_start_request.description: start_rsi(): developer starts an offline session on one eligible parent.

rsi_submit_request.description: submit_rsi(): publish the sealed incumbent as a Candidate. Reply is a bare Ref(Candidate).

rsi_resume_request.description: resume_rsi(): explicit human command after a security block. clearance_ref is the committed rsi_security_clearance SystemRef.

rsi_session_result.description: RsiSessionResult, a closed internal envelope. Optional fields are absent when not applicable. A security block also carries security_block_ref (checked by the controller).

rsi_attempt_entry.description: One immutable, hash-chained line of attempts.jsonl. entry_sha256 is the SHA-256 of canonical UTF-8 JSON of every other field. First entry has previous_entry_sha256=null. Comparison fields appear together or not at all; interrupted or rejected-before-query entries omit them.

rsi_trial.description: Payload of the private rsi_trial SystemRecord: implementation snapshot plus visible hard-gate evidence. Never hidden bytes; not a Candidate.

rsi_security_clearance.description: Payload of the rsi_security_clearance SystemRecord, written only by the authenticated human terminal.

rsi_verify_boundary_request.description: rsi.verify_boundary(profile_ref, fixture_manifest_ref); runs independently of optimization.

rsi_verify_boundary_report.description: Immutable report of one run of RSI-S01..RSI-S23 (the suite is run three times) plus the lifetime query attack (the 91st query, RSI-S24). result=pass requires every observed=PASS; NOT_RUN is never a pass.

trial_ref.description: Private rsi_trial reference {id, sha256}. Authorized namespace: controller evidence root only. Not a Candidate Ref.

oracle_ref.description: Private oracle control/result record reference {id, sha256}. Resolves only through the oracle's authenticated API.

oracle_begin_request.description: begin_session(): authenticated controller only. No fixture-pool ids, paths or cases.

oracle_status_request.description: status(): controller or custodian; no per-case detail.

oracle_session_result.description: SessionResult. session_id exists only after durable creation. For closing/closed, session_record_ref is the oracle_closure; otherwise the oracle_session.

oracle_evaluate_request.description: evaluate(): controller only. No final purpose is accepted here; the service chooses set and incumbent.

oracle_aggregate_result.description: AggregateResult. Complete carries every count, medians rounded to 10 ms, disposition, score hash and the redacted result_ref. Other states expose no counts. No per-case data crosses.

oracle_close_request.description: close_session(): seals proposals, fixes a zero-to-five ablation schedule.

oracle_finish_close_request.description: finish_close(): one result ref per scheduled ablation, in order; empty for an empty schedule.

oracle_final_request.description: evaluate_final(): custodian-only authenticated channel, once per closed session.

oracle_clear_security_request.description: clear_security(): human custodian channel only. clearance_ref is the terminal-written rsi_security_clearance SystemRef.

poc_execute_request.description: execute_poc(): runner-side benchmark capsule asks the process service to run generated code. The caller never chooses executable, host path, UID or network.

poc_execute_result.description: PocExecutionResult. A nonzero exit_code is workload evidence, not an infrastructure failure. Capture failure never returns exited.

measurement_request.description: measure_next on a descriptor bound to one reserved POC request. A repeated request_id returns the same sample.

benchmark_sample.description: One harness stdout line (BenchmarkSample), as returned by the measurement service.

measurement_result.description: Reply to measure_next. denied after the final scheduled sample.

measurement_evidence.description: Artifact value committed by the measurement service for each arm. Service-owned; no capsule-to-capsule wire uses it.

syntax_check_evidence.description: Output of syntax_check(), published as an Artifact.

deliver_request.description: Type-agnostic delivery call. Ordinary code, no Gate, no capsule. Publishes the listed terminal outputs verbatim under the destination.

publication_manifest.description: Committed record of every published file with its sha256 and source ref. Paths are unique.

deliver_result.description: Reply to deliver(): ref of the committed publication_manifest.

intake_request.description: launch(prompt, channel, workspace) as sent to the intake module by CLI or web. Intake qualifies it into an intake value and a source_text.

intake_result.description: Reply after intake recorded the intake and source_text artifacts.

resource_snapshot_request.description: snapshot_resources(): trusted supervisor service copies explicitly bound inputs into an owned read-only snapshot.

resource_snapshot_result.description: Committed snapshots, one per requested resource_id, published in one supervisor batch.

intent_fidelity_review.description: Independent fidelity review of a compiled intent_ir against the source text, produced by research.verifier with profile research.accept_intent.v1. Each of the six checks appears exactly once. result is the overall check outcome (pass, fail, unknown); it is not a Gate verdict. Errors carry source_quotes.

intent_repair_record.description: One bounded repair pass of research.compile_intent. generation is the new intent_ir.generation (1..4); repair_budget defaults to 1, hard cap 4.

evaluator_sha256.description: Hash of this manifest as pinned in rsi_session and oracle_session (evaluator_sha256).

scoring_rule_sha256.description: Hash of the frozen scoring rule: keep when wins>=1 and losses=0, tie-break by median duration at least 10 percent lower, final promotable only if losses=0 and the 5th percentile of Beta(1+wins,1+losses) exceeds 0.5.

split_hashes.description: Content hashes of the three splits. They must be pairwise different and hash-disjoint at the case level (checked by the oracle, not by this schema).

minimums.description: Pinned floors: at least 20 loop and 20 final cases, the parent fails at least 20 percent of each set, and at least 5 parent failures in the final set. A manifest may raise a floor, never lower it.

hash_registry_sha256.description: Hash of the commit-before-reveal registry (per-fixture sha256, set_sha256, count, frozen_at) merged before the first session.

evaluator_manifest.description: Private evaluator manifest, readable only by the oracle account and the custodian. It resolves the evaluator_sha256 pinned by begin_session to the oracle code, launcher, write guard, scoring rule, split hashes, the loop and final fixture set manifests, the planted-child corpus and the pinned models. It carries no case content. Missing or inconsistent pins refuse the session (fixture-oracle.md).

lineage_group_ids.description: Ids of the source groups the cases derive from; a group never spans two splits.

content_sha256.description: Hash of the sealed set; equals the matching split hash in the evaluator manifest.

case_sha256s.description: Hash of each fixture (case), in set order; one entry per case, so its length equals case_count. Hashes only, never the case.

headroom_evidence_ref.description: Fixture-author preflight evidence that the parent fails at least the pinned share of the set (headroom rule); null for a dev set.

fixture_set_manifest.description: Metadata of one sealed fixture set: its role, size, lineage groups and hash. It never carries case inputs, labels or expected answers. A loop or final set has at least 20 cases.

planted_child_manifest.description: The fixed planted-child corpus: at least ten known-bad child hashes (each must be rejected) and at least three known-good child hashes (each must be kept or promotable). The oracle must show the comparator behaves as expected on all of them before optimization is enabled.

expected_reason_codes.description: Reason codes the refusal must carry. Empty when the expected effect is "no effect on the result" (the attack is ignored).

rsi_attack_scenario.description: One entry of the violation suite (PRD 3.Y.11, formerly V1 to V23): RSI-S01 to RSI-S23, plus RSI-S24, the 91st lifetime query attack. Each scenario attacks on purpose and expects a refusal that is logged.

rsi_attack_result.description: Result of one attack run. observed PASS means the system refused with the expected reason code and the refusal is logged (evidence_refs lists the private audit and OS events); FAIL means it was not refused or the code differs; NOT_RUN means the scenario did not run and is never a pass. reason_code is the code actually observed, null when none was produced.
